stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Astronomers randomly selected 150 stars from a catalog of stars within 50 light-years of the Sun. They found that 32% of the selected stars have at least one known planet, with an associated margin of error of 6%. The astronomers then randomly selected 600 different stars from the same catalog and estimated the same percentage. The margin of error for the second sample was calculated the same way.
choices: The second sample's margin of error is expected to be greater than 6%.
The second sample's margin of error is expected to be less than 6%.
The second sample's margin of error is expected to be about 6%.
The second sample's margin of error is expected to be about 1.5%.
explanation: Both samples come from the same catalog and use the same method. The only difference is size: the second sample has 600 stars instead of 150. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error, so you should expect the second margin of error to be less than 6%. Because the sample is 4 times as large, the margin is divided by $\sqrt{4} = 2$, which gives about 3%.

A.why: You reversed the relationship. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error, not a larger one.

C.why: You treated the margin of error as fixed for the catalog. You missed that the sample size changed from 150 to 600, and that change shrinks the margin.

D.why: You divided 6% by 4 because the sample is 4 times as large. The margin of error is divided by the square root of 4, so it comes to about 3%, not 1.5%.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A sports scientist studied runners in a regional running league. She surveyed two random samples of the league's runners about whether they train with a heart-rate monitor. In Sample X, 55% of 80 runners said yes. In Sample Y, 45% of 320 runners said yes. The margin of error for each estimate was calculated the same way.
choices: Sample Y's estimate has the larger margin of error because Sample Y is larger.
Sample X's estimate has the larger margin of error because its percentage is higher.
The two estimates have the same margin of error because both samples are from one league.
Sample X's estimate has the larger margin of error because Sample X is smaller.
explanation: The two samples come from the same league and use the same method, so sample size is the only thing that matters here. Sample X has 80 runners and Sample Y has 320. The smaller sample gives the larger margin of error, so Sample X's estimate has the larger margin.

A.why: You reversed the relationship. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error, so Sample Y's margin is the smaller one.

B.why: You named the right sample but gave the wrong reason. The difference comes from sample size, not from 55% being higher than 45%.

C.why: You noticed that both samples come from the same population, but you ignored that one sample is 4 times the size of the other. That difference changes the margin of error.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A paleobotanist randomly selected 50 fossil leaves from a museum's collection of leaves from one quarry. Based on the sample, it is estimated that the mean length of the leaves in the collection is 6.2 centimeters, with an associated margin of error of 0.8 centimeter. The paleobotanist plans a new study of 200 leaves randomly selected from the same collection. The margin of error will be calculated the same way.
choices: The new margin of error will most likely be greater than 0.8 centimeter.
The new margin of error will most likely be equal to 0.8 centimeter.
The new margin of error will most likely be less than 0.8 centimeter.
The new mean leaf length will most likely be less than 6.2 centimeters.
explanation: The new study draws from the same collection and uses the same method, but it uses 200 leaves instead of 50. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error, so the new margin of error will most likely be less than 0.8 centimeter.

A.why: You reversed the relationship. More leaves give a smaller margin of error, not a larger one.

B.why: You ignored that the sample size grows from 50 to 200. A change in sample size changes the margin of error.

D.why: You applied the effect of sample size to the estimate instead of the margin of error. A larger sample makes the margin smaller, but it does not push the sample mean in any particular direction.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Labor economists studied employed adults in the city of Riverton. They surveyed two random samples about whether the adults work from home at least one day a week. In the first sample, 38% of 1,200 adults said yes, with an associated margin of error of 2.8%. In the second sample, 41% of 300 adults said yes. The margin of error for the second sample, $m$, was calculated the same way.
choices: $m$ is greater than 2.8%, because the second sample is smaller.
$m$ is less than 2.8%, because the second sample is smaller.
$m$ is greater than 2.8%, because 41% is greater than 38%.
$m$ is equal to 2.8%, because both samples are from Riverton.
explanation: The second sample has 300 adults instead of 1,200, and it comes from the same population and uses the same method. A smaller sample gives a larger margin of error, so $m$ is greater than 2.8%.

B.why: You reversed the relationship. A smaller sample gives a larger margin of error, not a smaller one.

C.why: You reached the right inequality but for the wrong reason. The difference in margins comes from sample size, not from 41% being higher than 38%.

D.why: You noticed that both samples come from Riverton, but you ignored that the second sample is a quarter the size of the first. That difference changes the margin of error.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A nutrition scientist ran a pilot study of 40 randomly selected students at one university. Based on the sample, it is estimated that the students' mean daily fiber intake is 18 grams, with an associated margin of error of 3 grams. The full study will use 400 randomly selected students from the same university. The margin of error will be calculated the same way.
choices: The full study will likely have a margin of error smaller than 3 grams.
The full study will likely have a margin of error larger than 3 grams.
The full study will likely have a margin of error of about 0.3 gram.
The full study's estimate will likely apply to students at every university.
explanation: The full study uses 400 students instead of 40, from the same university and with the same method. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error, so the full study's margin will likely be smaller than 3 grams. Because the sample is 10 times as large, the margin is divided by $\sqrt{10}$, which gives about 0.95 gram.

B.why: You reversed the relationship. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error.

C.why: You divided 3 by 10 because the sample is 10 times as large. The margin of error is divided by $\sqrt{10}$, so it is about 0.95 gram, not 0.3 gram.

D.why: You applied the result to a population that was never sampled. Every student in the study comes from one university, so the conclusion only covers that university.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: Folklore researchers asked randomly selected adult residents of a mountain region whether they could retell a local legend about a ghostly ferryman. In Survey A, 64% of 250 residents could retell it, with an associated margin of error of 6%. In Survey B, 58% of 1,000 residents from the same region could retell it. The margin of error for Survey B was calculated the same way.
choices: Survey B's interval of plausible values is likely wider, because Survey B included more residents.
Survey B's interval of plausible values is likely narrower, because Survey B's percentage is lower.
Survey B's interval of plausible values is likely narrower, because Survey B included more residents.
Survey B's interval of plausible values is likely the same width, because both surveys used one region.
explanation: The interval of plausible values is the estimate plus or minus the margin of error, so its width depends on the margin. Survey B has 1,000 residents instead of 250, from the same region and with the same method. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error, so Survey B's interval is likely narrower.

A.why: You reversed the relationship. More residents give a smaller margin of error, which makes the interval narrower, not wider.

B.why: You reached the right conclusion but for the wrong reason. The interval is narrower because of the larger sample, not because 58% is lower than 64%.

D.why: You noticed that both surveys come from the same region, but you ignored that Survey B is 4 times as large. That difference changes the margin of error.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: City planners want to estimate the percentage of households in the Eastgate district that support adding protected bike lanes. They can afford one of two surveys: 150 randomly selected Eastgate households or 600 randomly selected Eastgate households. The margin of error would be calculated the same way for either survey. The planners want the estimate with the smaller margin of error.
choices: They should use the 150-household survey, because a smaller sample gives a smaller margin of error.
They should use the 600-household survey, because a larger sample gives a smaller margin of error.
They can use either survey, because sample size does not change the margin of error.
They should use the 600-household survey, because its result would apply to the whole city.
explanation: Both surveys draw from the same district and use the same method. The larger sample gives the smaller margin of error, so the planners should choose the 600-household survey.

A.why: You reversed the relationship. A smaller sample gives a larger margin of error.

C.why: You ignored the one thing that differs between the two surveys. The margin of error depends on sample size, and 600 is 4 times 150.

D.why: You chose the right survey for the wrong reason. Only Eastgate households would be sampled, so the result applies to Eastgate and not to the whole city.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A bird-banding station keeps records of every warbler it has captured. Volunteer A randomly selected 120 of these records and found that 45% of the birds were juveniles, with an associated margin of error of 9%. Volunteer B randomly selected 240 records from the same database and found that 52% were juveniles. The margin of error for Volunteer B's estimate was calculated the same way.
choices: Volunteer B's margin of error is most likely greater than 9%.
Volunteer B's margin of error is most likely about 4.5%.
Volunteer B's data show that most of the station's warblers are juveniles.
Volunteer B's margin of error is most likely less than 9%.
explanation: Both volunteers sampled the same database with the same method, and Volunteer B used twice as many records. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error, so Volunteer B's margin is most likely less than 9%. Doubling the sample divides the margin by $\sqrt{2}$, which gives about 6.4%.

A.why: You reversed the relationship. A larger sample gives a smaller margin of error.

B.why: You assumed that doubling the sample halves the margin of error. The margin is divided by $\sqrt{2}$, so it comes to about 6.4%, not 4.5%.

C.why: You treated 52% as exact. With a margin of error of about 6%, the plausible range runs from below 50% to above 50%, so the data don't show that most of the warblers are juveniles.
